caption: What if you could clone yourself? A clone is a genetic copy of you, with the same DNA. But here's the catch: a clone is born as a baby, so your 'copy' would be decades younger than you. Dolly the sheep, born in Scotland in 1996, was the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, and she was the only lamb out of 277 attempts. Your memories aren't stored in DNA, so your clone wouldn't know your friends, your jokes or your passwords. Nature already makes near-clones: identical twins. Yet even twins have different fingerprints. In 2009, scientists at NDRI Karnal cloned a buffalo calf named Garima. Human reproductive cloning, though, is prohibited under India's research guidelines, as in many countries. Plot twist: CC, the first cloned cat, didn't even have the same coat pattern as her donor. Would YOU want a clone of yourself? 👇
